MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  June 26, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 6:00 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird. Council recessed to
Closed Session at 6:01 PM.

  •  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Pursuant to Government Code § 54956(b)
  Number of potential cases: 3
  Potential claims arising from Bluff Cove Homes licenses and current uses

Council reconvened to Open Session at 7:40 p.m.

City Attorney Hogin reported that the Council took no reportable action in Closed Session;
however, the matter was continued to July 2, 2012 at 5:30 p.m. in Chambers of City Hall.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT:  Mayor Bird, Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, Councilmember Humphrey,
  Councilmember Perkins, Councilmember Rea

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg, City
  Treasurer Sherwood, City Attorney Hogin, Asst. to City Manager Davis,
  Asst./Deputy City Clerk Kroneberger

CEREMONIAL MATTERS

  •  Recognition of Retiring Traffic Safety Committee Chair Myron A. Friedman (Mayor Bird)

Mayor Bird said Mike Friedman, a long time Palos Verdes Estates resident, started his volunteer
service to the City as a member of various financial advisory committees. In July 2003, Mr.
Friedman was appointed to the Traffic Safety Committee; served as Vice- Chair from 2006 to 2009,
and Chair from 2009 to June 2012.

During his service, the Traffic Safety Committee was instrumental in the implementation of a
variety of stop signs, restriping, turn restrictions and other important safety measures implemented
CITY COUNCIL
June 26, 2012

  1
 at PV Intermediate School as student enrollment and related traffic issues grew, and was also
responsible for key aspects the Residential Parking Zone (RPZ) implementation which addressed
serious congestion issues to the neighborhood immediately surrounding Palos Verdes High School.

Mayor Bird thanked Mr. Friedman for his ten years of service on the Traffic Safety Committee and
presented Mr. and Mrs. Friedman with an engraved crystal paperweight commemorating the City’s
gratitude.

Mr. Friedman thanked the Mayor and City Council.

Each of the Council members thanked Mr. Friedman with personal remembrances for his service,
his love for the community, his selfless contribution of time and expertise, setting a good example,
and making the City a better place.

9.  RESOLUTION R12-14; APPROVING THE AUDITOR'S REPORT AND SETTING
  THE FIRE AND PARAMEDIC SERVICES SPECIAL TAX RATE FOR FY 2012-13

City Manager Smith reported that the current contract runs through June 2016, which has been
financed with a 10-year special tax passed in 2007 with 87% voter approval. The annual increase
in the fire service costs is capped by the contract. The maximum cost increase for FY12-13 would
have been 3.89%, while the proposed contract cost represents a 3.87% increase. The total contract
for FY 12-13 is $4.131 million; the majority of which is for personnel and benefits related to the
staffing of Station 2 and County overhead. The special tax rate is also capped. The Council
directed that the annual auditor’s report be prepared using a 3.5% increase in the tax rate, which
will generate approximately $4.15 million. For FY 07-8 through 10-11, the annual increase was
4.2%. Last year, there was no increase because the fire contract cost did not increase. She said the
median home will pay $729.05 or $1.99/day for fire and paramedic services. She said the funds are
restricted and are used only for fire and paramedic services related costs.

 On motion of Humphrey, seconded by Perkins, Council approved Resolution R12-14; Approving
the Auditor's Report and Setting the Fire and Paramedic Services Special Tax Rate for FY 2012-13
by unanimous oral vote.

10.  ADOPTION OF THE FY 2012-13 BUDGET:  RESOLUTION R12-15;
  ESTABLISHING THE FY 2012-13 APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT, AND R12-16
  ADOPTING THE ANNUAL BUDGET AND FIXING THE LIMITATION OF
  EXPENDITURES

City Manager Smith reported that these two resolutions are the final steps required to adopt the
budget for FY 12-13. Resolution R12-15 approves the City’s appropriations limit (Gann Limit) for
actual expenditures that can be financed through tax proceeds. Using the adjustment factors
(increase in per capita personal income and population) the appropriations limit for FY12-13 is
$18.1 million. Actual tax proceeds expected total $12.5 million. Resolution R12-16 represents
authorization of operating and capital budgets totaling $17.75 million; exhibits include
expenditures by funds, authorized and number of positions, and salary ranges for FY 12-13.

On motion of Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Rea, Council approved
Adoption of the FY 2012-13 Budget: Resolution R12-15; Establishing the FY 2012-13
Appropriations Limit, and R12-16 Adopting the Annual Budget and Fixing the Limitation of
Expenditures by unanimous oral vote.

CITY COUNCIL
June 26, 2012

  4
 11.  PUBLIC SAFETY REALIGNMENT, AB 109 AND RELATED BILLS, AND THE
  IMPACT ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY

Chief Dreiling reported that the Prison Realignment Bill (AB 109) contains provisions which
constitute the most significant changes to our criminal justice system in the State’s history. The
high rate of criminal recidivism (currently at 67.1%), the State budget shortfall of $26 billion, and
prison overcrowding are addressed in the bill that was signed into law July 2011. There were
numerous bills that followed to amend discrepancies, and pursuant to a Supreme Court ruling, these
provisions will ultimately be in full effect by July 2014, when the state prison population must be
reduced to 137.5% of design capacity.

Captain John Eberhard reported that the bills amend the definition of felony to include
imprisonment in a county jail for more than one year; those that qualify for county jail sentences
are classified as N3 felons: non-serious, non-violent, and non-high risk sex registrants (Non’s).
The bills also enhance the authorization granted for correctional administrators; L.A. County Board
of Supervisors authorized Sheriff Baca to release prisoners to involuntary home detention programs
using monitoring devices. As of July 2013, counties will monitor parolees, except those on parole
for life sentence. Post-release community supervision (PRCS) will be handled by the probation
dept. Governor Brown has introduced a ¼ cent tax increase (November 2012 ballot) to pay for the
associated costs, as well as trying to augment vehicle license fees.

Chief Dreiling said in order for the County to absorb an influx of inmates, the Sheriff will be forced
to free up jail space by availing himself of these various release provisions. Chief Dreiling said
some parolees will be given probation (reclassified as Non’s); 108,000 current inmates are
currently on parole and this bill seeks to reduce that number to 30,000 under the post release
community supervision program (PRCS); violators will be returned to County jail. The State penal
system will be reduced, allowing the population to be reduced by attrition. He said we will feel the
affect of the presence of PRCS’s as they populate our neighboring communities. Chief Dreiling
said PVEPD will assume an aggressive and proactive stance and will be watching for violations of
post release. PD Supervisors are actively developing strategies and are working with other
departments to gather and share intel, and with Neighborhood Watch to bolster membership.

Councilmember Perkins was appreciative of the report and asked how the department will become
aware when someone is to be released into our community. Chief Dreiling said the County will
notify us 120 days prior to release, and we will have reciprocal agreements with other
communities.

Councilmember Perkins asked if residents will have this knowledge. Chief Dreiling said some of
the Non's are available on the Megan’s' Law registry; some information will be available, high risk
offenders will not be classified as Non’s.

MPT Goodhart said the state will benefit by the reduced cost, but it is unknown what the county
costs will be going forward and the jail system is already expensive. He asked what the recidivism
rate of N3 felons. Chief Dreiling responded that total recidivism is high; in the San Francisco area,
it is 75%; locally, 67% of offenders return to prison.

CITY COUNCIL
June 26, 2012

  5
 Chief Dreiling said the state releases parolees, some will be reclassified as Nons; 8600 will be
released on probation in L.A. County in January. Then the problem becomes supervision. PVEPD
will visit those in and close to our community (PRCS's). 47 deputies shall be authorized by the
Sheriff’s Department to supervise the post releases; we are Region 3 of 8 county regions. Seven
deputies will cover our large region.

MPT Goodhart confirmed with Chief Dreiling that the solution is to work with other agencies to
provide adequate supervision. Councilmember Humphrey said probation is in lieu of something
else; supervising those parolees is a concern. Captain Eberhard said added training will be required
to monitor those that were once to be paroled.

Councilmember Rea asked about the possibility of increased use to our city jail. Chief Dreiling
said PVE is a Class 2 jail, and can only house prisoners for 48 hours. Councilmember Rea asked if
the law will permit the county to outsource to out-of-state private facilities. Chief Dreiling said
private institutions are being looked at and the law doesn't prohibit the county from doing this; but
this wouldn't have the same beneficial budget affect as the 3 prong approach as contained in
AB109.

Councilmember Humphrey commended the report, but it’s still a big concern, and Neighborhood
Watch will become extremely important.

Mayor Bird said residents enjoy superb protection from our P.D., with less than 2 minutes in
response time. It is incumbent on residents to step up and join and participate in Neighborhood
Watch. All residents are encouraged to participate; applications are available from Community
Relations Officer McCullough and at City Hall. He encouraged residents getting to know their
neighbors; we all need to be aware of what goes on in our community. Mayor Bird said burglaries
are common in PVE and Chief Dreiling encouraged calls to P.D. when something suspicious
occurs in a neighborhood; P.D. will check it out.

Councilmember Perkins said residents can submit ‘vacation check’ request forms to the Police
Department for extra patrols when a resident is on vacation or away; PD Reserves also patrol
homes. MPT Goodhart suggested that the CRO advise residents of this service through
Neighborhood Watch.

Mayor Bird asked about solicitors/solicitations rules. Chief Dreiling explained the City’s permit
application process.

The report was received and filed.

Other Reports:

Mayor Bird reported that he and City staff met in the City Manager’s office on June 13th with
Marvin Jackmon, Southern California Edison rep, who provided an update on equipment upgrades
in the area, and noted that very few outages have occurred since his last report. On June 16th, the
Mayor Bird provided a welcome message to attendants at the American Cancer Society Relay for
Life.

Mayor Bird reported on his attendance at the June 20th Lunada Bay Homeowners Association
Annual Meeting and congratulated Peter Bena on his installation as Board President.

Mayor Bird reported on his attendance at a meeting with the 4 City concessions on June 21st at City
Hall, with MPT Goodhart, to discuss mutual opportunities and disaster preparedness.

MPT Goodhart reported on his attendance at the League of California Cities Environmental Policy
Committee meeting in Sacramento on June 14th--budget trailer bills, VLF funds; and efforts of
California Forward were among the topics of focus.

Councilmember Perkins reported on her attendance at a meeting of the Santa Monica Bay
Restoration Commission on June 21st on behalf of the COG. The discussion focused on the
Japanese tsunami debris that has started to appear along the Pacific coast; Malaga Cove Beach was
selected amongst local coastline areas being monitored. She also attended the 50th Anniversary
Celebration of the Malaga Cove Post Office Building with Councilmember Humphrey.
